items.title: Second Fractional Order Differential Constitutive Relations for Viscoelastic Materials of the Fractional Type with Piezoelectric Properties, Representing Rheological Models of Higher Complexity Levels
items.abstract: The author presents newly derived differential constitutive relations (equations) of the second fractional order for complex, higher-level rheological models of fractional-type viscoelastic materials with piezoelectric properties. These newly derived differential equations are of the second fractional order and incorporate Caputo differential operators of the first and second fractional orders. The lecturer outlines an approximate analytical methodology for solving these second-fractional-order differential equations, employing the Laplace transform, expansion into power series with respect to the complex Laplace parameter, and the properties of the convolution of three functions. This methodology yields approximate analytical solutions for the mew derived second-fractional-order differential constitutive equations governing these complex, higher-level rheological materials. These approximate analytical solutions simultaneously serve as integral constitutive relations, establishing the link between normal stresses and axial strains in these complex, higher-level rheological models of fractional-type viscoelastic materials with piezoelectric properties. The theoretical analytical results obtained pertain to complex fractional-type material models, specifically the second-level complexity Letherish-Faraday model for a fractional-type viscoelastic material with piezoelectric properties; The Jeffreys-Faraday model represents a second-level complexity rheological model for a fractional-type viscoelastic material with piezoelectric properties, while the Burgers-Faraday model represents a third-level complexity model of the same type. These three rheological models of higher complexity—in their classical linear forms—are already widely used; the author believes that the newly introduced fractional-type models (named by the author) will also see widespread application, initially in the validation of experimental research and subsequently in practical use. The lecturer also believes that these results open up new challenges regarding the development of software for calculating inverse Laplace transforms of complex Laplace-transformed expressions, thereby expanding the scope of artificial intelligence in areas where it is currently underdeveloped and limited.

items.title: Secondary School Teachers’ Interaction with Artificial Intelligence Systems: A Qualitative Investigation of Usability, Trust, and the Transformation of the Pedagogical Role
items.abstract: This research explores secondary education teachers" perceptions regarding the integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into instructional practice. Through semi-structured interviews with a sample of ten (10) educators from diverse academic backgrounds, the study examines three core pillars: interaction and usability, issues of trust and ethics, and the transformation of professional identity. The findings reveal that using AI tools is a complex cognitive process requiring strategic prompt engineering. Despite the small sample size, participants consistently demonstrated a "cautious acceptance," acting as critical evaluators of machine-generated outputs to mitigate scientific inaccuracies and "hallucinations." In conclusion, the study highlights a shift in the teaching role from being a source of knowledge to an authority of critical mediation. It emphasizes the urgent need for professional development that fosters pedagogical agency and ethical action within the modern digital learning environment.

items.title: Semantic Communications and Edge Intelligence in 6G Wireless Networks: Task-Oriented Joint Source-Channel Coding and Latency Bounds
items.abstract: Abstract—As cellular architectures transition from 5G toward Sixth-Generation (6G) wireless networks, the classical Shannon-Nyquist paradigm of bit-level data transmission is rapidly approaching its theoretical physical channel capacity limits. Ultra-dense Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems, autonomous vehicular swarms, and extended reality (XR) telepresence demand terabit-per-second (Tbps) data rates, sub-millisecond latencies, and continuous real-time edge artificial intelligence (AI) inference over severely bandwidth-constrained wireless channels. Classical communications optimize bit error rates (BER), transmitting massive streams of uncompressed binary representations regardless of the underlying computational task. Semantic Communications and Task-Oriented Edge Intelligence establish a transformative paradigm shift: shifting the transmission objective from error-free bit reconstruction to the faithful transmission of actionable semantic meaning and task-relevant latent features. By uniting Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding (Deep JSCC) with transformer-based feature extractors, semantic communication frameworks filter out redundant sensory data at the transmitter, communicating only task-critical representations to edge compute nodes. However, deploying semantic communications over stochastic wireless channels introduces acute foundational challenges: semantic noise induced by channel fading, joint training instability across non-differentiable wireless channels, and catastrophic performance degradation under out-of-distribution physical channel shifts. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of semantic communications for 6G edge intelligence. We formalize the rate-distortion-perception tradeoff under Weaver-Shannon semantic communication tiers, model continuous-time Deep JSCC over Rayleigh and Rician fading channels, and establish Lyapunov-guided end-to-end latency bounds for distributed edge inference. Furthermore, we construct an empirical software-defined radio (SDR) and GPU testbed evaluating multimodal perception and edge autonomous vehicle telemetry under severe signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) degradation. Our empirical findings demonstrate that Deep JSCC semantic transmission achieves a 78.4% reduction in required channel bandwidth while preserving 94.6% downstream edge classification accuracy under extreme channel noise (SNR = -6 dB), where classical JPEG/264 paired with LDPC coding completely collapses. Finally, we formulate open research directions in semantic knowledge base synchronization, neuro-symbolic semantic verification, and zero-trust semantic cybersecurity. Index Terms—Semantic Communications, 6G Wireless Networks, Edge Intelligence, Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding (Deep JSCC), Task-Oriented Communications, Shannon-Weaver Levels, Physical Layer AI.

items.title: Service Recovery in Chatbot‐mediated Environments: Trust Dynamics and Customer Loyalty Intentions
items.abstract: Abstract Prior research has shown that customers’ perceptions of chatbots may be influenced by the situational context in which human–chatbot interactions take place. This research advances understanding of artificial intelligence (AI)‐enabled chatbot‐led service failure recovery (SFR) in the context of customer loyalty. Using a social constructivist philosophical perspective and an inductive approach, 52 in‐depth interviews were conducted to capture individuals’ perceptions of chatbot‐led interactions during a SFR process and how these perceptions impacted their trust in, and commitment to, brands. Utilizing commitment‐trust theory and trust transfer theory, we propose a framework that characterizes the relationships between a chatbot‐led SFR process and customer loyalty intentions. Based on the emergent data, customers’ evaluations of a service recovery journey led by chatbots can be grouped into four main outcomes: continued trust in, and commitment to, chatbot and brand; continued trust in, and commitment to, brand; discontinued trust in, and commitment to, chatbot; and discontinued trust in, and commitment to, chatbot and brand. Our findings extend current understanding of how consumers’ trust and commitment during chatbot‐led interactions during SFR evolve and highlight the dynamic relationship between consumers and the context of interactions. This study has theoretical and practical implications for developing and leveraging customers’ loyalty in AI‐enabled chatbot‐led SFR environments.

items.title: Sharenting as a Parenting Practice and the Recognition of the Child's Agency: A Transactional Analysis Perspective
items.abstract: This article examines sharenting practices among parents in relation to the recognition of the child's agency and the underlying relational mechanisms, interpreted through the lens of Educational Transactional Analysis (ETA). The empirical study employed a questionnaire-based survey of N = 420 parents of children aged 6-15 attending primary schools in Poznań, Poland. Statistical analyses (Welch's t test, Pearson's χ² test) revealed a digital privacy paradox: despite widespread endorsement of children's right to privacy, as many as 61.6% of parents of children aged 6–15 do not always ask their children for consent before publishing their image, or do not always respect their answers. This practice illustrates the discounting of the child's digital sovereignty from a paternalistic life position. Mothers were more likely than fathers to approach sharenting relationally, seeking digital strokes through the Child ego state. Higher self-assessed knowledge co-occurred with stronger concerns about artificial intelligence and with a propensity for corrective action (41.7% of parents had deleted previously posted photos of their child). The shift toward a position that recognizes the child as a subject occurs in response to adolescents' resistance or to parental self-reflection. The pedagogical implications point to the need for workshops on relational digital maturity and for promoting digital consent from the earliest years.
